title: docs(qa): 18.0 sweep anchor round 20 — the area fixture recipes name the own-port boot by its port and file DB
body:
Refs #24579
Clause-②: no

Round 20 of the 18.0 sweep's wave anchor (claim `6307282355`, PM loop round 35). It applies round 19's carried finding, PR #25027's out-of-scope finding as its ACCEPT `6306169987` and landing record `6306857223` carry it.

Only checklist text changes: 11 strings in the area-level `fixtures` recipes of four area files, five recipes in all. No item changes, no top-level key other than those recipe strings moves, and there is no product code, test, pin, changeset text or `RUNNER.md` edit.

- Base `d68aab6fde` (`origin/main` when the branch was cut). `origin/main` has since moved one commit to `dfe60e3a0c`, which touches only `packages/core` and a changeset, none of it cited by the ledger.
- Head `60fccd21ef`, one commit.

## The recording rule, as read

`docs/qa/platform-checklist/README.md` gives a recipe no revision or history of its own. The recipe shape ("Half 1 — the recipe") lists `$comment`, `title`, `why`, `provenance`, `app`, `requires`, `sequence`, `teardown` and `knownGaps`. `revision` and `history` are item fields: the Lifecycle section's "Change" rule ("edit the fields, bump `revision`, append a `history` entry") is about items. The validator's own comment says the same ("recipes carry no `revision`/`history` of their own", `scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs`), and none of the five recipes on disk carries either key. So only the strings are edited here. No revision field is added, and no item's `revision` or `history` moves.

## What changed

The respelling uses the voice rounds 17–19 landed: "an isolated boot (own port + file DB, …)" becomes "a boot on its own port and file DB (…)", matching `access-security`'s round-17 rows. "discard the isolated file DB … an isolated boot makes free" becomes "discard the run's own file DB … a boot on its own port and DB makes free", matching `platform-core.manifest-install-contract` `steps[9]`, round 17. Each parenthetical keeps the dogfood section-0 pointer as its file spelled it ("dogfood skill §0" or "dogfood §0"). Only the fragments below change; the rest of each string is byte-identical.

| file | recipe | field | old → new |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `attachments-storage.json` | `qa-scratch-authz` | `requires[2]` | `an isolated boot (own port + file DB, dogfood skill §0)` → `a boot on its own port and file DB (dogfood skill §0)` |
| `attachments-storage.json` | `qa-scratch-authz` | `teardown` | `discard the isolated file DB, … the one an isolated boot makes free` → `discard the run's own file DB, … the one a boot on its own port and DB makes free` |
| `attachments-storage.json` | `qa-media-constraints` | `requires[1]` | `an isolated boot (own port + file DB, dogfood skill §0)` → `a boot on its own port and file DB (dogfood skill §0)` |
| `attachments-storage.json` | `qa-media-constraints` | `teardown` | `discard the isolated file DB, the cheaper path an isolated boot makes free` → `discard the run's own file DB, the cheaper path a boot on its own port and DB makes free` |
| `automation.json` | `qa-flow-status-doors` | `requires[1]` | `an isolated boot (own port + file DB, dogfood §0)` → `a boot on its own port and file DB (dogfood §0)` |
| `automation.json` | `qa-flow-status-doors` | `requires[2]` | `(RUNNER.md, the isolated-boot/OS_PORT standing fact)` → `(RUNNER.md, the own-port/OS_PORT connector standing fact)` |
| `automation.json` | `qa-flow-status-doors` | `teardown` | `discard the isolated file DB, the cheaper path an isolated boot makes free` → `discard the run's own file DB, the cheaper path a boot on its own port and DB makes free` |
| `records-forms.json` | `qa-feeds-disabled` | `requires[1]` | `an isolated boot (own port + file DB, dogfood skill §0)` → `a boot on its own port and file DB (dogfood skill §0)` |
| `records-forms.json` | `qa-feeds-disabled` | `teardown` | `discard the isolated file DB, … the one an isolated boot makes free` → `discard the run's own file DB, … the one a boot on its own port and DB makes free` |
| `search.json` | `qa-contributor-bound-member` | `requires[2]` | `an isolated boot (own port + file DB, dogfood §0)` → `a boot on its own port and file DB (dogfood §0)` |
| `search.json` | `qa-contributor-bound-member` | `teardown` | `discard the isolated file DB — the cheaper path an isolated boot makes free` → `discard the run's own file DB — the cheaper path a boot on its own port and DB makes free` |

`git diff --stat`: 4 files, 11 insertions, 11 deletions.

**The re-pointed pointer (`qa-flow-status-doors.requires[2]`).** RUNNER.md's connector entry is now titled "A boot on its own non-3000 port breaks the showcase's self-pinging connectors unless you export `OS_PORT` …". The new pointer names it by words that title carries: own, port, `OS_PORT` and connector. "standing fact" is kept, because it is the section's own word: the entry sits under "Environment facts the runner should not re-derive", whose intro calls them "Standing facts about the stock showcase environment". The sibling item text `automation.json` already uses the same form ("RUNNER.md's connector self-URL standing fact").

## `isolated` left in the four files' recipes

Read over every string under each file's top-level `fixtures` block, the `$comment` annotations included, at the head:

| file | recipe · field | text | sense | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| all four | every recipe string | the word `isolated` | — | none left: 16 at the base, all inside the 11 strings above; 0 at the head |
| `records-forms.json` | `qa-feeds-disabled` · `sequence[1].expect` | "a caller who can read and edit this parent isolates FEEDS_DISABLED from the sibling RECORD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE refusal" | the verb: tells one refusal apart from another | kept (names neither the boot nor the posture) |

No posture text was in any of the five recipes, so none was touched.

**Items citing a changed recipe string verbatim: none.** Every area file's items were searched for each old fragment. Three history rows carry the same phrasing: `access-security.rls-both-sides` and `access-security.record-share-grant-revoke` `history[6]`, and `platform-core.manifest-install-contract` `history[5]`. Each quotes its OWN item's old step text, not a recipe string, so nothing is reported under that rule. Outside `areas/`, `git grep` finds no file quoting any old fragment.

## How the edits were made and checked

A one-off script (sha256 `52f33dacca5c…`, kept out of the tree) tokenizes each file to the byte span of every string value by JSON path. It edits only the 11 named spans and re-encodes each new value in the file's own style. It never re-serialises a file. Its assertions, all run in a dry run and again on the bytes re-read from disk after `--write`:

- each span round-trips (decoding the span equals the parsed value, and re-encoding reproduces the span);
- each phrase replacement hits exactly its expected count, and no edited string keeps `isolat`;
- the new file parses, with the same set of string-value paths;
- the new document equals the old one with only the 11 paths replaced: `items` equal, every other top-level key equal, every other recipe equal, and every other field of an edited recipe equal;
- every byte outside the edited spans is identical, the head, the gaps and the tail included (trailing-newline state too);
- each file's `isolat` count drops by exactly the named strings' hits (6, 4, 3, 3).

The assertions were shown to fire first: three faults injected into the in-memory result (an item title edit, a whitespace-only change outside the spans, an edit to an unnamed recipe field) were each caught by the intended assertion. A separate per-file count against the base agrees: each old fragment goes from N to 0 and each new one from 0 to N, in the same files.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derives 13 commands on the 4 paths, against merge base `d68aab6fd` of `origin/main`. At head `60fccd21ef` each was run with its exit code captured before any pipe, and each exited 0:

`node scripts/check-ci-filter-parity.mjs` · `node scripts/check-closing-keyword-parity.mjs` · `node scripts/check-closing-keyword-parity.mjs --self-test` · `node scripts/check-comment-mask-corpus.mjs` · `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint run check:doc-formula-expressions` · `pnpm check:cross-package-test-inputs` · `pnpm check:doc-authoring` · `pnpm check:driver-memory-census` · `pnpm check:gitlink-declared` · `pnpm check:nul-bytes` · `pnpm check:platform-checklist` · `pnpm check:refd-timer-probe` · `pnpm check:watch-hint-literal`

The first run of `check:doc-formula-expressions` refused with exit 3, a prerequisite: `@objectstack/formula` and `@objectstack/lint` were not built in this worktree. Both were built under the shared verify lock (`VERDICT command-exit 0`, a full turbo cache replay, held 1 s, waited 0 s), and the rerun exited 0. `--ran`, with an exit code on every line, reads "13 derived, 13 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN", a derived zero.

No per-PR CI job runs `pnpm check:platform-checklist`, so this local reading is its evidence. The base column was taken in this worktree at the base, before any edit:

| reading | base `d68aab6fde` | head `60fccd21ef` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| exit | 0 | 0 |
| items | 16 areas, 328 items (323 active, 1 planned) | 16 areas, 328 items (323 active, 1 planned) |
| provisioning | 5 area recipes, 10 item references resolved (2 area-qualified), 5/5 recipes referenced | 5 area recipes, 10 item references resolved (2 area-qualified), 5/5 recipes referenced |
| line citations | 0 survive across 21 swept documents | 0 survive across 21 swept documents |
| symbol anchors | 979/989 against 434 cited sources, 10 on the named residual (#16898), 18 file floors held | 979/989 against 434 cited sources, 10 on the named residual (#16898), 18 file floors held |

No anchor, citation or recipe key is added or removed. `main`'s one later commit touches no file the ledger cites.

`git merge-tree --write-tree` exited 0 against each of:

- `origin/main` `dfe60e3a0c`;
- PR #25024's head `356172a1f9` (its only `docs/qa/` file is `FOLLOW-UPS.md`).

None of these paths is routed to the `os-regen` merge driver (`merge: unspecified`).

There is no ablation, because no tested behaviour changed. `skip-changeset` was re-measured. No `files[]` entry of the 73 non-private manifests (86 tracked `package.json` files) reaches outside its own package or names `docs/qa`, and the repo root is private. The two `docs/qa` mentions under `packages/` (`service-settings` `config-change-audit.ts`, and `packages/lint`'s gate script) are comments, not copies. A grep of the built dists on disk for the edited recipe keys finds none, with a positive control hit in `packages/spec/dist`.

## Acceptance notes

- **`automation.flow-error-handling` `fixtures.requires[0]`** (an item, not on this round's surface) says `api.example.com` is "unroutable from the isolated env, so the failure is deterministic". That `isolated` means the network-isolated (no-egress) environment. It is a third sense: neither the own-port boot nor the tenancy posture. Noted, not filed; no carrier.
- **`qa-contributor-bound-member.requires[2]`'s pointer** "(RUNNER.md's connector self-URL fact)" is left as it was. "connector" is a word of the entry's title and "self-URL" names its resolver, and the ruling named only `qa-flow-status-doors`'s pointer for re-pointing.
